Laozi on contentment

Laozi (traditionally 6th century BCE) approaches contentment within Daoism. It describes the Dao as the generative way of things and recommends wu wei, flexible action that does not force outcomes. Systematically, the teaching links Dao, non-action, simplicity into a practical and theoretical whole. On this page, the archive isolates English passages where that project meets contentment most directly—useful for searches such as “laozi quotes on contentment.”

How to use this page

Start with the shortest passage, then compare tone across sources. Return to the Laozi thinker page for biography and to the contentment theme for other voices on the same question.

  1. One who knows others is wise; one who knows oneself is enlightened. One who conquers others has strength; one who conquers oneself is truly strong. One who knows contentment is rich; one who persists has will.
    Q0159
    Daodejing, Ch. 33
  2. Know contentment, and you will not be disgraced; know when to stop, and you will not be imperiled — thus you can endure.
    Q0163
    Daodejing, Ch. 44
